title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity, from international agreements on asteroid missions to significant funding rounds for emerging players. Meanwhile, traditional defense contractors are busy securing lucrative contracts, and the Space Force is gearing up for a new leadership era.

themes.title: International Collaborations Heat Up
themes.body: ESA and JAXA's finalized agreement on the Apophis asteroid mission marks a notable step in global space cooperation. Paraguay's signing of the Artemis Accords further indicates a growing interest in joining the lunar exploration club.

themes.title: Defense Contracts on the Rise
themes.body: Viasat's $307 million contract with the Marine Corps underscores the ongoing demand for satellite communications in military operations. Meanwhile, Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program shows that data management remains a hot commodity.

themes.title: Emerging Players Securing Funding
themes.body: True Anomaly's $190 million Series C funding round highlights the appetite for innovative space startups. Similarly, Skyroot's emergence as India's first space unicorn signals a shift in the global investment landscape.

themes.title: Leadership Changes in Space Force
themes.body: The nomination of Lt. Gen. Douglas A. Schiess as the next Chief of Space Operations suggests a strategic pivot for the Space Force. As the organization evolves, its focus on AI and operational readiness will likely shape future initiatives.
